Activity – Measures of Variation
Dataset A:
10, 12, 14
Dataset B:
5, 10, 21
Task for Students
○
Calculate the Range for each dataset.
○
Calculate the Mean for each dataset.
○
Compute the Variance.
○
Compute the Standard Deviation.
○
Which dataset is more spread out?
Solution 
Dataset A: 10, 12, 14
Mean
(10 + 12 + 14) ÷ 3 = 36 ÷ 3 = 12
Range
14 – 10 = 4
Variance
(10−12)² = 4
(12−12)² = 0
(14−12)² = 4
(4 + 0 + 4) ÷ 3 = 8 ÷ 3 ≈ 2.67
Standard Deviation
√2.67 ≈ 1.63
Solution 
Dataset B: 5, 10, 21
Mean
(5 + 10 + 21) ÷ 3 = 36 ÷ 3 = 12
Range
21 – 5 = 16
Variance
(5−12)² = 49
(10−12)² = 4
(21−12)² = 81
(49 + 4 + 81) ÷ 3 = 134 ÷ 3 ≈ 44.67
Standard Deviation
√44.67 ≈ 6.68

Why Standard Deviation Matters in ML
If you were building a model,
which dataset is more predictable?
Dataset A
Example
●
Dataset A:
8, 10, 12
●
Dataset B:
2, 10, 18
●
Calculate the Mean for both datasets.
●
Calculate the Range.
●
Which dataset is more spread out? Why?
Solution 
Dataset A:
8, 10, 12
Mean
8 + 10 + 12 ÷ 3 = 30 ÷ 3 = 10
Range
12 −8 = 4
The values are close to the mean, so the data is tightly clustered.
Solution 
Dataset B:
2, 10, 18
Mean
2 + 10 + 18 ÷ 3 = 30 ÷ 3 = 10
The mean is the same as Dataset A.
Range
18 −2 = 16
The values are far from the mean, so the data is more spread out
Conclusion
●
Both datasets have the same mean (10).
●
Dataset B has a much larger spread.
●
Therefore, Dataset B has a larger standard deviation.
●
The mean tells us the center, but the standard deviation tells us how spread 
out the data is

Outlier Detection Rule
Lower Bound:
𝑄1 −1.5 × 𝐼𝑄𝑅
Upper Bound:
𝑄3 + 1.5 × 𝐼𝑄𝑅
Any value outside this range is considered an outlier.
